title: OS binding: script steps
description: Scripts in scope bound to specific operating systems through Claris script steps: curated OS affinity from the official documentation (there is no structured Claris OS table; absence of a statement means 'Claris states nothing', never 'runs everywhere'). Covers 'exclusive' steps (Perform AppleScript -> macOS, Send DDE Execute -> Windows), source-true inverse 'unsupported' statements resolved against the host OS of the step's runtimes (Dial Phone 'not supported in macOS' => Windows + iOS, never Linux), and the Send Event dual-variant (one step id, two OS-exclusive option sets; the only behavior-variant with a findings row - the other variants stay schema-viewer knowledge). The os_profile uses the set-wide vocabulary (macos-only, windows-only, desktop-only, apple-only, ios-only, desktop-variant, mixed). 'ios' is the OPERATING SYSTEM (FileMaker Go and iOS SDK apps), never the Go runtime chip. Inventory, not defects - findings are neutral properties, never errors.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: An OS-bound script step binds every calling script to that OS: Perform AppleScript is silently ignored on Windows, Send DDE Execute on macOS - the runtime compatibility table cannot see this (it lists both steps as plain 'Pro'). The curated OS affinity makes the invisible OS story explicit.
rule.remediation: Nothing to fix. Use the inventory to know which scripts assume which OS; guard OS-bound steps with Get(SystemPlatform) checks where a script must run cross-platform.
